governedKillSwitchAuthorityRepair.rootCause: STRUCTURAL. production-shadow-authorization.ts imports cutover-mode.ts, so cutover-mode.ts -- which produces the authoritative enablement answer -- could not consult the kill switch without a circular import. The brake was therefore only ever reachable from modules DOWNSTREAM of the authority decision, and release binding and provenance assignment are not downstream of it: they are two of its four consumers.
governedKillSwitchAuthorityRepair.repairDesign: The emergency stop was extracted to the new import-free module standards/cutover/cutover-kill-switch.ts, below cutover-mode.ts in the dependency graph, and applied inside resolveCutoverEnablement() -- the single canonical answer to 'may this customer request enter governed mode right now?'. No kill-switch check was added to any consumer: four independent interpretations of one variable is the shape that produced the defect.
governedKillSwitchAuthorityRepair.rejectedAlternative: Inlining the environment read into cutover-mode.ts would have kept that module import-free but duplicates the parse and leaves the in-process RUNTIME LATCH -- the one the circuit breaker pulls with no operator present -- unable to stop governed authority at all.

canonicalSemantics.notOverloaded: MODE_IS_LEGACY and NO_ALLOWLIST_CONFIGURED are NOT reused; both describe a configuration that was never governed, and reporting either during an incident would send an operator to fix something that did not change.

rootCauses.RC1_outcome_field_order: `outcome` was the FIRST property in the wire schema. Structured decoding emits properties in schema order, so the producer committed to whether there was anything to add BEFORE enumerating a single hazard. Hosted R1/R5 returned every collection empty in 635 and 254 output tokens; the local baseline returned NOTHING_TO_ADD on 27 of 27 calls INCLUDING calls that populated three collections. Nothing validated outcome against content, so this was invisible from section 99 until now.
rootCauses.RC2_wire_weaker_than_boundary: Required strings had no minLength (an empty string passed STRICT transport validation and was then refused at the boundary as CANDIDATE_MALFORMED -- section 104's R6); crossHazardInsights.participants had no minItems while the boundary requires >=2 (refused insights emptied the collection and left the interaction in the summary, an EXPLANATION_ONLY_LOSS manufactured by an under-specified schema rather than by a model that failed to reason); and evidence was not required at all.
rootCauses.RC3_contract_instructed_omission: Grounding was not merely optional. The prompt said 'BUT A QUOTE IS OPTIONAL ... raise the candidate anyway with an empty evidence list' and the schema description repeated it, so silence was the cheapest legal answer and every producer took it -- quotes=0/0 across 14 local calls in sections 100/101 and EVIDENCE_QUOTES_EMITTED=0 across both hosted grounding fixtures in section 104. NOT model incapacity: the same local model emitted exactly-bound quotes as soon as the contract stopped inviting it not to.
rootCauses.RC4_negative_control_over_routing: NO STRUCTURAL CAUSE ESTABLISHED. minLength explains the CANDIDATE_MALFORMED half of HG12. The over-production half is prompt-pressure asymmetry, which is a HYPOTHESIS and not a measurement, and it is NOT claimed as repaired. The local model kept both negative controls empty 10/10 before and after, so it cannot falsify the hypothesis either way.

contractChanges.analysisContractVersion: hazlenz.expert.analysis.v2 -- UNCHANGED. The wire form moved; the normalized contract the customer path consumes did not.
contractChanges.outcomeMovedLast: From the FIRST property to the LAST, after the typed lists, the explanation and the uncertainty -- a consequence of the lists rather than a commitment preceding them, and the order the system prompt has asked for since section 99.
contractChanges.minLength: minLength:1 on every required string, so the transport refuses what the boundary would refuse.
contractChanges.groundingStatus: Required enum on hazard candidates: EXACT_QUOTE_SUPPLIED (evidence must be non-empty and every quote must bind exactly) or NO_EXACT_QUOTE_AVAILABLE (evidence must be empty; the candidate SURVIVES and scores as ungrounded). `evidence` is now required beside it.
contractChanges.whyThisIsNotAttempt1: Section 101 attempt 1 demanded a QUOTE from every candidate, so a candidate the model could not quote had no legal shape and the whole collection vanished. Here the model must always DECLARE, and NO_EXACT_QUOTE_AVAILABLE with an empty list is a fully legal candidate that still reaches the reviewer. What is no longer legal is SILENCE -- omission now costs a falsifiable claim about the observation.
contractChanges.internalTypeUntouched: groundingStatus is deliberately NOT added to ExpertHazardCandidate. Grounded/ungrounded stays derivable from `evidence`, so there is no second copy of the same fact to drift.
contractChanges.newReasonCodes: GROUNDING_STATUS_INVALID (item-level: bad formatting); GROUNDING_CLAIM_UNSUPPORTED (item-level: the declaration and the evidence disagree in EITHER direction); OUTCOME_INCONSISTENT_WITH_CONTENT (recorded, NOT rejected and NOT corrected -- this module resolves and refuses, it does not rewrite a producer's output).
contractChanges.staleAssertionsReAnchored: A.13/A.15 in test-expert-routing-contract asserted the v3 rule that evidence is NOT required. That went STALE exactly as G14 did in section 103.4. They were RE-ANCHORED, not deleted or loosened: the property they protect -- an unquotable hazard is RAISED, not dropped, so section 101's suppression cannot return -- now has a DIRECT assertion. Suite 57 -> 58 assertions; nothing that used to fail now passes.

decisionsReversedByMeasurement: GROUNDING_CLAIM_UNSUPPORTED was ANALYSIS-FATAL first, by analogy with EVIDENCE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS. The local probe measured the cost: 9 of 10 grounding iterations returned NOTHING AT ALL, good clarifications and insights destroyed alongside the one candidate that lied -- section 101's suppression in a new costume, and the same lesson expert-normalization.ts already records from L3-2i. Now ITEM-LEVEL, which does not weaken the rule (the lying candidate still does not cross at all) and which this phase's authorization names in as many words: 'must fail closed OR remain non-authoritative'.

maxLength:120 on quotedText was added to stop the local model pasting the whole observation into a quote, and REMOVED after measurement: under that provider's structured decoding it produced not a shorter span but a TRUNCATED one, cut mid-sentence with stray characters appended, which bound LESS often than the over-long quote it replaced. A schema keyword that corrupts output on a provider we can actually test is not a repair.

HISTORICAL.evidence: inferConditionState() reaches HISTORICAL through five branches. FOUR OF FIVE stamp correctionStatus 'reported' and state in their own currentCondition text that the current status or exposure is NOT established; only the 'described as corrected' branch stamps 'verified'. The frozen definition of CORRECTED requires the observation to assert the hazard was PUT RIGHT, so mapping the other four to CORRECTED would tell Expert the hazard was fixed exactly where the engine said it could not establish the current status -- a false statement, not an approximation.
HISTORICAL.whyInsufficientEvidenceNotUnknown: The engine DID establish something -- a prior condition is documented -- and failed only on the current state; and the engine's own UNKNOWN branch (reported-but-unverified correction) must stay distinguishable in the Expert view.

PLANNED_FUTURE.whyAmbiguous: The engine asserts a SCHEDULED activity ('planned but not yet underway'); the frozen definition of HYPOTHETICAL is CONTINGENT framing (if / were / would / could / might). A scheduled activity satisfies 'no present occurrence' and FAILS 'contingent'. No member of the eight-state vocabulary means 'scheduled but not yet begun' -- a vocabulary gap, not a choice between readings.
PLANNED_FUTURE.alternativeA: HYPOTHETICAL (carried forward from section 121, currently in code). Right in effect, wrong in kind. Risk: Expert reasonably declines to raise a hazard that IS going to occur.
PLANNED_FUTURE.alternativeB: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Reports an uncertainty that does not exist, since the engine settled the state. Risk: invites a clarification on a row that owes none, pushing against M10's 0.15 ceiling.
PLANNED_FUTURE.measuredMitigation: ZERO of the 45 eligible reserved rows exercise it. Across all 100 reserved rows the engine produced 92 ACTIVE, 1 HISTORICAL and NO PLANNED_FUTURE, so the decision changes nothing for the material in hand.

hsH1Adjudication.determinationVerbatim: The general concern that load thermal state may remain hazardous despite zero chamber pressure is valid. The authored cooling-hold selector is not uniquely supported because the observation does not establish the load type, cycle type, manufacturer/SOP unload criteria, or that a cooling hold is the applicable safe-unloading mechanism. Zero chamber pressure/interlock release does not establish safe liquid-load temperature, but absence of a cooling hold does not by itself establish that opening must stop for every possible load.

hsH1Adjudication.generalisedTest: A selector naming a specific mechanism is uniquely supported only when the observation establishes the conditions under which that mechanism is the applicable one. Failing to settle the safe state is not the same as establishing which mechanism governs it.

expertHazlenzVerifierDrawReliability2026.semanticResidue: THE DECISIVE LIMIT. On HS-A1, 7 of 10 draws asked a well-formed, plausible safety question about a DIFFERENT fact — auger lockout — rather than the human target. On HS-E1, 8 of 10 fell silent. Neither failure is a reliability failure that repetition can fix: repeating a draw resamples the same distribution, and that distribution is centred on the wrong answer on BOTH cases. Reliability policy can raise the chance that something is asked; it cannot make the verifier ask the right thing. A bounded reliability policy is therefore worth having and is NOT sufficient on its own.

remediationHypothesis.narrowestTarget: prompt-level only: instruct Expert that a verification stated at a PAST occasion does not establish the state at the moment the decision is made, so a positively-stated but stale verification is an unresolved fact. Nothing else — not the schema, not the normalizer, not the verifier, not arbitration, not thresholds.
remediationHypothesis.risk: this is a recall repair and recall repairs cost precision. HR-05 already shows the model over-asking about an adjacent unsettled source, so any change must be measured on the SILENCE half before it is believed. A repair that lifts recall to 5/5 while dropping precision below 4/5 is not an improvement.

expertHazlenzTemporalClarificationRemedi.rootCause: The §175 HR-04 miss was not the model ignoring an instruction — it was the model FOLLOWING one. "CURRENT STATE, NOT HISTORICAL STATE" tells it not to re-litigate a stated verified fact, and HR-04 stated one: the fastenings had been torque-checked. What the prompt never said is that a verification speaks for a TIME and the decision may depend on a different one. The repair is therefore placed at the boundary of the rule that produced the silence, not bolted on elsewhere.

It states the rule (a verification is scoped to its moment), gives the operative procedure (compare the two moments), and resolves rather than hedges when they match.
brakesInTheSameBullet: THIS IS ABOUT THE DECISION, NEVER ABOUT AGE
no schedule, due date or routine period makes evidence stale or fresh
a verification performed long ago is FULLY ESTABLISHED where the decision does not depend on a later moment
a verification performed minutes ago settles nothing about a state that changed after it
three named non-reasons: record is old, interval has elapsed, re-checking would be good practice
and the five-part counterfactual test must still be met in full

answers.Q1_owedFactRepresentation: OPTION C — reuse acceptableEvidence.requirement, which is already 'one sentence naming the capability the evidence must establish'. answers.Q2_settlementDeclaration: YES, split across layers — deterministic projection supplies the target, the provider supplies evidence observed / property established / assessment / reason, the verifier checks FORM only, and human review is the sole authority that can convert a claim into SETTLED_BY_EVIDENCE. answers.Q3_settlementStates: keep OWED_FACT_STATUSES closed at four. Statuses are authority-bearing and no authority produces 'partially established'. EVIDENCE_PROPERTY_MISMATCH and TEMPORAL_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED are valuable as open-text REASONS, which decide nothing, and brittle as statuses.

answers.Q5_displacedValidFactControl: the control ALREADY EXISTS — every declaration must bind to a key in the closed set or nominate with a full structural proof burden across 24 admission codes — and it was not running in §179. Settlement state adds observability (fact A settled while fact B nominated becomes countable), never suppression; any rule suppressing adjacent nominations is explicitly rejected.
answers.Q6_acceptableEvidenceInteraction: role unchanged. Null projects as explicit absence, a claim against it is flagged SETTLEMENT_CLAIMED_WITHOUT_GOVERNED_CRITERION and cannot reach SETTLED_BY_EVIDENCE. answers.Q7_governedKnowledgeGap: EVIDENCE_QUESTION_TO_VERIFICATION_METHOD_ALIGNMENT classified PARALLEL_REMEDIATION with the AUDIT half recommended early. answers.Q8_customerQuestionBudget: settlement removes questions that were never owed, which is categorically different from deferring questions that are. It must NOT be used to justify combining facts into one string — one question, one factKey, unchanged. No production threshold defined.
answers.Q9_observability: record the comparison, not just the verdict: owed requirement beside claimed property, evidence span, provenance class, assessment, reason, admission codes, final status and authority, binding and nomination origin, coverage state.
